title: ASSIGNMENT – 3
subtitle: TCP Client–Server Applications for Checksum- and CRC-Based Error Detection
name: Srikrishna O S

sections.heading: AIM
paragraph: To develop two TCP client-server applications in Python for error detection over the network. Assignment 3a protects online banking transactions using the 1's Complement Checksum technique: the client computes the checksum of the data words and sends data plus checksum to a threaded bank server, which verifies integrity before processing. Assignment 3b protects video frames in a smart city traffic surveillance system using the Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) technique: the client computes the CRC remainder by XOR division with a generator polynomial, appends it to the frame, and a threaded monitoring server re-divides the received frame and accepts it only if the remainder is zero.
Both applications simulate transmission errors (error-free, single-bit, multiple-bit, and burst) so the effectiveness of each technique can be analyzed.

rows: One bit flipped in each word

sections.heading: LEARNING OUTCOMES
bullets: I computed the 1's complement checksum with carry wrap-around and bitwise inversion.
I implemented CRC generation and verification using XOR long division in Python.
I built threaded TCP servers that verify integrity before processing data.
I detected single-bit, multiple-bit, and burst errors with both techniques.
I concluded that CRC catches burst errors well and suits multimedia and real-time traffic data.
I observed that a print lock is needed when multiple client threads log to the same console.
